User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user on the platform.

oldUserId.description: Stored username if the user changes their username.

photoURL.description: URL to the user's profile picture.

preferredCurrency.description: The user's preferred fiat currency for display.

isBanned.description: Indicates if the user is banned by an administrator.

isOnHold.description: Indicates if the user's account is on hold (lien).

tradeVolume.description: Total trade volume of the user (auto-calculated).

completedTrades.description: Number of completed trades by the user (auto-calculated).

usernameChanged.description: Indicates if the user has changed their username (max once).

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the user account was created.

lastTradeAt.description: Timestamp of when the user's last trade was completed.

lastLoginIp.description: IP address of the user's last login.

UserWallet.title: UserWallet
UserWallet.description: Represents a user's wallet for a specific cryptocurrency.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user wallet.

balance.description: Current balance of the cryptocurrency in the wallet.

lockedBalance.description: Amount of cryptocurrency locked in trades or other operations.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of when the wallet balance was last updated.

id.description: Unique identifier for the deposit request.

userDisplayName.description: Denormalized username of the user making the deposit.

crypto.description: Cryptocurrency type deposited (e.g., BTC, ETH, USDT).

txId.description: Transaction ID of the deposit on the blockchain (optional).

walletAddress.description: The crypto address the user needs to deposit to.

qrCodeUrl.description: The URL of the QR code for the deposit address.

status.description: Status of the deposit (pending, approved, declined, expired).

timerEnd.description: Timestamp when the deposit timer ends.

adminId.description: Reference to Admin. (Relationship: Admin 1:N Deposit). ID of the admin who approved or declined the deposit.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the deposit request was created.

CryptoDepositAddress.title: CryptoDepositAddress
CryptoDepositAddress.description: Stores the deposit address and QR code for a specific crypto and chain, managed by admins.

id.description: Unique identifier for the withdrawal request.

userDisplayName.description: Denormalized username of the user making the withdrawal.

crypto.description: Cryptocurrency type withdrawn (e.g., BTC, ETH, USDT).

status.description: Status of the withdrawal (pending, approved, declined, cancelled).

adminId.description: Reference to Admin. (Relationship: Admin 1:N Withdrawal). ID of the admin who approved or declined the withdrawal.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the withdrawal request was created.

P2PAd.title: P2PAd
P2PAd.description: Represents a P2P advertisement for buying or selling cryptocurrency.

id.description: Unique identifier for the P2P ad.

publicAdId.description: Public, user-friendly identifier for the P2P ad.

crypto.description: Cryptocurrency type being traded (e.g., BTC, ETH, USDT).

fiatCurrency.description: The fiat currency for the trade.

paymentMethods.description: Payment methods accepted for the trade.

ratePercent.description: Percentage adjustment to the market rate (if applicable).

fixedRate.description: Fixed rate for the cryptocurrency (if applicable).

terms.description: Terms and conditions of the ad.

active.description: Indicates if the ad is active.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the ad was created.

Trade.title: Trade
Trade.description: Represents a trade between a buyer and a seller.

buyerId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N Trade). ID of the buyer.

sellerId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N Trade). ID of the seller.

adId.description: Reference to P2PAd. (Relationship: P2PAd 1:N Trade). ID of the ad associated with the trade.

crypto.description: Cryptocurrency type being traded (e.g., BTC, ETH, USDT).

amount.description: Total amount of cryptocurrency in the trade.

fiatCurrency.description: The fiat currency for the trade.

fiatAmount.description: The total fiat amount for the trade.

price.description: The price per crypto unit at the time of the trade.

status.description: Status of the trade (active, paid, released, expired, disputed, cancelled).

claimedByBuyer.description: Indicates if the buyer has claimed the released funds.

paymentReceiptUrl.description: URL of the uploaded payment receipt from the buyer.

paidAt.description: Timestamp when the buyer marked the trade as paid.

releasedAt.description: Timestamp when the seller released the cryptocurrency.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the trade was created.

TradeChat.title: TradeChat
TradeChat.description: Represents a chat message within a trade.

id.description: Unique identifier for the chat message.

senderId.description: Reference to User. ID of the user who sent the message.

mediaUrl.description: URL of the media file attached to the message (optional).

isModerator.description: Indicates if the message was sent by a moderator.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the message was sent.

Dispute.title: Dispute
Dispute.description: Represents a dispute opened for a trade.

openedBy.description: Reference to User. ID of the user who opened the dispute.

status.description: Status of the dispute (open, resolved, cancelled).

resolvedBy.description: Reference to Admin. (Relationship: Admin 1:N Dispute) ID of the admin who resolved the dispute.

winnerId.description: ID of the user who won the dispute.

resolutionNote.description: Notes on how the dispute was resolved.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the dispute was created.

Feedback.title: Feedback
Feedback.description: Represents feedback given for a completed trade.

fromUser.description: Reference to User. ID of the user giving the feedback.

toUser.description: Reference to User. ID of the user receiving the feedback.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the feedback was created.

AdminLog.title: AdminLog
AdminLog.description: Represents an action performed by an administrator.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin log.

adminId.description: Reference to Admin. ID of the administrator performing the action.

targetId.description: ID of the target entity (e.g., User ID, Trade ID) affected by the action.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the action was performed.

PaymentMethod.title: PaymentMethod
PaymentMethod.description: Represents a payment method available for trading.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment method.

name.description: Name of the payment method (e.g., UPI India, Bank Transfer USA).

country.description: Country where the payment method is primarily used (e.g., India, USA).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and easily debuggable, adhering to the core design principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). Authorization Independence is achieved through denormalization, where authorization-relevant data is copied into subcollections to avoid using `get()` calls in security rules. Structural Segregation is employed to ensure that all documents in a collection share the same security requirements, simplifying rules and improving security posture.

*   **Users Collection:** `/users/{userId}` stores user profiles. This is private user data, accessible only to the user themselves. The `userId` is used as the document ID, enforcing path-based ownership.
*   **User Wallets Subcollection:** `/users/{userId}/wallets/{walletId}` stores wallet information for each user. The wallet documents inherit access control from the parent `users` document, as the wallets are owned by the user. Denormalization is NOT required here because of the path-based ownership.
*   **Deposits Subcollection:** `/users/{userId}/deposits/{depositId}` stores deposit requests initiated by the user. Similar to wallets, access is controlled by the parent `users` document, ensuring only the user and admins can access the deposit information.
*   **Withdrawals Subcollection:** `/users/{userId}/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}` stores withdrawal requests made by the user. The same path-based ownership applies.
*   **Notifications Subcollection:** `/users/{userId}/notifications/{notificationId}` stores user-specific notifications. Access is strictly limited to the owning user.
*   **P2P Ads Collection:** `/p2p_ads/{adId}` stores P2P ad listings. The `userId` of the ad creator is denormalized into each document to allow for simple security rules based on ownership without needing to read from the `users` collection. This supports QAPs by enabling secure `list` operations based on ownership or other ad attributes.
*   **Trades Collection:** `/trades/{tradeId}` stores trade information. The `buyerId` and `sellerId` are denormalized into each document, so that security rules can easily check if the requesting user is either the buyer or the seller. This is critical for Authorization Independence. `adId` also exists on each document for data reasons.
*   **Trade Chat Subcollection:** `/trades/{tradeId}/messages/{messageId}` stores chat messages for each trade. Access is controlled by checking if the user is either the buyer or seller of the parent `trades` document. The subcollection enforces that only trade participants can access the chat.
*   **Disputes Subcollection:** `/trades/{tradeId}/disputes/{disputeId}` stores dispute information for trades. Access is restricted to the involved parties and admins. Similar to `trade_chats`, the `tradeId` enforces a hierarchical access pattern.
*   **Feedback Subcollection:** `/trades/{tradeId}/feedback/{feedbackId}` stores feedback for trades. The parent `tradeId` ensures that feedback is only associated with valid trades, and access is limited to the trade participants.
*   **Admin Logs Collection:** `/admin_logs/{logId}` stores logs of admin actions. Only admins have access to this collection. Access to this collection is granted based on the existence of a document with the admin's UID in the `/roles_admin/{uid}` collection.
*   **Support Tickets Collection:** `/support_tickets/{ticketId}` stores user support requests. Writable by any signed-in user, but only readable and manageable by admins.
*   **Payment Methods Collection:** `/payment_methods/{paymentMethodId}` stores a list of acceptable payment methods for the platform.
*   **Admin Roles Collection:** `/roles_admin/{uid}` stores documents indicating admin status. The existence of a document at this location grants admin privileges.  This approach (Existence over Content) simplifies security rules and improves performance.

This structure facilitates simple and robust security rules by leveraging path-based ownership where applicable, and denormalizing authorization data where necessary to eliminate `get()` calls.  The explicit structure and naming conventions enhance debuggability and maintainability.
